title: Kaleidos: Policy-weighed SLO rollback advisor for multi-metric rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Implement an advisor service (Kaleidos) that synthesizes multiple SLO signals (latency percentiles, 5xx error-rate, token cost per request, throughput) into a single, explainable rollback decision signal. Kaleidos should be callable from rollout controllers (canary, A/B, shadow) and support both hard aborts and soft-suppress traffic actions. This is intended to reduce manual error-prone rollback tuning and give product teams predictable automated behavior for model rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Kaleidos exposes a gRPC/REST endpoint that returns a decision: KEEP | SOFT_LIMIT | ABORT and an explanation payload (list of top-3 contributing signals).
Decision latency < 50ms in production traffic path (cold start excluded).
Default policy achieves <1% false-positive abort rate in 10 simulated canary experiments derived from production traces.
Policy parameters are annotated in runtime-1.22 release notes and editable from Console rollouts UI under 'Safety policies'.
End-to-end integration test with canary controller demonstrates traffic throttle instead of abort for soft-thresholds in 80% of simulated transient spikes.
technical_notes: Design summary: Kaleidos computes a per-cohort weighted z-score for each metric: latency_p95, error_rate_5xx, token_cost_per_1k_tokens, QPS. Each metric is normalized by a rolling baseline window (configurable; default 30m) and by an interquartile-stable variance estimator to tolerate heavy tails. A policy-weigher maps product-defined importance into a weight vector w. The final composite score S = sum_i w_i * capped_sigmoid(z_i, cap=4). We have two thresholds: T_soft (traffic-suppress, default S>0.9) and T_hard (immediate abort, default S>1.6). Hysteresis: decisions require the condition to persist for a decay-window (configurable minutes) with burst-suppression using an exponential-backoff counter to avoid reacting to brief anomalies. Cost-awareness: token_cost is normalized to a cost-per-token z and multiplied by a cost_weight that dynamic-scales based on the customer's Dedicated vs Hosted tier. Explainability: response returns top-3 signals by contribution and time-series snippets (raw values) for debugging. Runtime: implemented as a sidecar-capable stateless service with an in-memory ring buffer for baselines; persistent baselines stored in time-series DB (Prometheus/TSDB) for rehydrate after restart. Safety knobs: emergency bypass, per-customer whitelist, and sandbox mode for A/B tests.
decisions: Use weighted z-score aggregation instead of Bayesian posterior fusion for initial rollout — chosen for explainability and easy tuning by PMs.
Expose both SOFT_LIMIT and ABORT outputs so Console can choose traffic-shaping vs immediate evacuation.
Default baseline window = 30 minutes and decay-window = 3 minutes. Tunable per-project in Console.
Keep token_cost as a first-class signal with a separate cost_weight that scales with customer tier (hosted vs dedicated).
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket filed after post-mortem 2026-02-25 highlighted inconsistent canary aborts across teams. Initial design and success criteria recorded.
2026-03-03: Prototype z-score aggregator implemented (ENG spike PR #142). Local sim harness shows improved explainability vs our previous boolean-rules baseline.
2026-03-05: Benchmarked decision latency on c5.large-like instance; median=12ms, p99=38ms. Memory footprint < 32MB for 50 cohorts. Added ring buffer rehydrate path.
2026-03-07: Integration tests with canary controller (PR #198) pass in sandbox. Observed two false-positive aborts on high-p75 traffic bursts; added burst-suppression backoff counter.

2026-03-10: Ran 10 simulated historical rollouts from Jan-Feb traces. Soft-limit behavior stopped 7/10 transient spikes without requiring abort; remaining 3 had sustained cost+latency regressions and triggered ABORT as expected. Preparing Console UI controls and docs for security review.
Next: finalize rollout knobs in Console and request security approval for RBAC on bypass keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for z-score normalization, capped_sigmoid, and contribution ranking.
Integration tests: canary controller must act on KEEP/SOFT_LIMIT/ABORT signals in staging rollout flows.
Chaos tests: inject spiky synthetic traffic (10-60s bursts) and verify soft-limit prevents ABORT > 90% of bursts.
A/B experiment: enable Kaleidos in 'audit-only' mode for 2 weeks on 5% of internal traffic and compare decisions vs current manual thresholds.
Load test: 5000 requests/sec decision queries from rollout controller to ensure <50ms median decision latency at scale.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (audit-only): 5% internal traffic, decisions logged but no action (2 weeks).
Stage 1 (soft-action): 10% of canaries use SOFT_LIMIT actions in staging (1 week).
Stage 2 (opt-in): Gradually enable policy for low-risk customer projects (10 projects) with default T_hard increased by 20% (2 weeks).
Stage 3 (default-on): Enable for all non-enterprise Hosted rollouts; enterprise/Dedicated remain opt-in with custom cost_weight (post security sign-off).
Emergency rollback: ops can flip 'force-abort' flag and bypass Kaleidos; documented in incident runbook.
